chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from more than one, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a female slave from another man with a condition (of warranty) for a day or two days, and she died while in his possession, and the price had been paid. He asked: 'On whom is the liability?' He (the Imam) said: 'There is no liability on the buyer until his condition (period of warranty) expires.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules of liability for a buyer if a purchased slave dies within the warranty period?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* from the chain of Aban ibn Uthman, this hadith clarifies the transfer of risk (daman) in sales contracts by establishing that the buyer bears liability only after the agreed warranty period expires. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that contractual conditions take precedence in determining when ownership risks shift from seller to buyer. It serves as a foundational precedent for modern commercial law regarding conditional sales and defect warranties.
